author: Tiana Maxwell
title: Greensboro Youth Town Hall aims to find solutions to youth violence - NewsBreak
text:
By Tiana Maxwell ,
54 minutes ago
GREENSBORO, N.C. (WGHP) — Greensboro city leaders and youth-focused organizations are hoping to find solutions to youth violence.
City leaders held a Youth Town Hall on Wednesday to hear directly from young people about what they need for a safer community. The meeting runs on a monthly basis.
Greensboro man has home after 10 years unhoused due to new Greensboro housing initiative: ‘Thought I was dreaming’ The city's 19-year-old Youth Engagement Director Jeremiah Jett said recent violence pushed a greater need for Wednesday's town hall. Recent incidents include a shooting that injured a teen at the Royal Banquet Hall on West Gate City Boulevard in early August.
"A lot of people just want to be young," Jett said. "You only get to be young one time and to be young and not feel safe at the same time is really a big problem."
Jett led the conversation with a series of questions that fall under the theme, "What does it mean to be safe in Greensboro?" Greensboro Police were present in the conversation. Jett said their participation is more than necessary.
"I don't think it's too far stretched to put us in a room with GPD and us be on the same playing field," Jett said. "And have those conversations, especially with everything that is going on. I think it'll be great for young people to see like, What does it look like from the GPD side? How can young people do our job, but also how can we let GPD know that they can be more of a partner with us?"
Jett said he takes the feedback from the meetings to create a 90-day action plan.
"What I do with that 90-day action plan is, I act on it, I build connections, talk to people, connect with different individuals" Jett said. "And my main thing is I don't want to just collect the data and then the young people are like, 'I went to this town hall, I was heard but nothing was done.'"
